testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: Can be exceeded when it is cooler outside.
Is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
Must be written in shipping papers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a given pressure. This rating is shown on the side of each tire.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes before slowing down. This makes your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you.

questions.question: Which gas is a problem if your exhaust system leaks?
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide into the cab or sleeper berth. Carbon monoxide is poisonous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing another driver, bicyclist, or pedestrian, always assume they do not see you. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving with the intent to harm or assault others
Operating a vehicle that is unsafe
Operating a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving with the intent to harm or assault others
questions.explanation: Road rage is driving with the intent to harm others or physically assault another driver or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is driving in a selfish or pushy manner.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect braking distance?
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase both striking power and braking distance. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, the braking distance becomes four times longer.

questions.question: Your CDL will be revoked if:

options.text: You want to add an endorsement.
Your license to drive your personal vehicle is revoked.
You have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license to drive your personal vehicle is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your license to drive is revoked, suspended, or canceled due to moving traffic violations, your CDL is also lost. This does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Roads with black ice look wet, not icy. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If a load is 40 feet long, it needs at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: One way to prevent fatigue on long trips is to:
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving through the night or when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before driving, look under it to find:

options.text: If the vehicle is on a hill.
Any fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
If the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or objects in the way.

questions.question: Oversized loads:

options.text: Can never be transported by a truck.
Should only be transported during the day.
Must have proper authorization to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must have proper authorization to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are oversized, over-length, or overweight.

questions.question: If you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, you:

options.text: Will likely complete the turn safely.
May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Can expect other drivers to move for your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before starting your left turn. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not let an aggressive driver provoke you. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle on any uphill grade. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed:

options.text: Are usually heavy enough and do not need to be strapped down.
Do not need to be strapped down if you drive slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off.

questions.question: To keep normal stopping power, set your front brake limiting valve to:
questions.explanation: Some vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep it in the "normal" position. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, you must:

options.text: Place a sign on the back of your vehicle.
Give up your CDL for six months.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should rise gradually to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test, you:

options.text: Do not need to use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
Must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
Can use any type of vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take your CDL skills test, including the on-road test, using the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.

questions.question: If a vehicle comes with an inspection report:

options.text: The driver should inspect the vehicle first, then compare their notes to the report.
The driver should read the report first when starting an inspection.
The driver should skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver should read the report first when starting an inspection.
questions.explanation: Always read any inspection report from the previous driver before you start your own vehicle inspection.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not dangerous because it is stopped.
Is only dangerous if passengers are getting off.
Is dangerous whether or not you can see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is dangerous whether or not you can see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby even if you cannot see them. The bus may block your view or their view of you.

questions.question: When should you upshift? The two signs are:
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. First is engine speed (rpm). Read your vehicle manual to learn the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is vehicle speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down:

options.text: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
Turn on one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Before you slow down, flash your brake lights by tapping your brake pedal lightly several times. This warns the drivers behind you that you plan to slow down.

questions.question: Aggressive driving means:

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with concern for other drivers' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving is operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy way without regard for the safety and rights of other road users.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down. Turn on your flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver when they are speaking.

questions.explanation: A hands-free phone is safer than a hand-held phone, but it still distracts your mind. Talking on any phone takes your focus away from driving.

questions.question: Before a trip, check your windshield. You should NOT:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check that the wipers have proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Check your windshield for cracks or damage. Check that the wiper arms have proper spring tension. Look for damage on the wiper blades, stiff rubber, and loose fasteners.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, check belts to make sure they are:
questions.explanation: Check all belts in your vehicle for tightness and wear.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear. Know how much movement is normal for each belt.

questions.question: As a truck driver carrying a load, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments along your intended route of travel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments along your intended route of travel.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for inspecting cargo, recognizing overloading or poor weight balance, making sure cargo is secured and does not block your view, and ensuring cargo does not restrict access to emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: What can happen if the air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: If you press and release the brake pedal too many times, air leaves the system faster than the compressor can replace it. Air brakes can stop working if pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Water that has collected on a roadway can cause:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are not safe to be used.
Are acceptable only when traveling at speeds under 40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to be used.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: When should you slow for a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause a skid.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used, as they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings at all times.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs required to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo on flatbed trailers. Always use at least two tie-downs no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should start the turn:

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
No sooner than the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No sooner than the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before starting your left turn. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle because of how the rear wheels track differently from the front.

questions.question: One way to avoid becoming an aggressive driver is to:

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Set realistic expectations regarding travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set realistic expectations regarding travel time.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays to avoid frustration that leads to aggressive driving. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, avoiding hand gestures at other drivers, and keeping both hands on the steering wheel.

questions.question: Fire extinguishers and other emergency equipment are:

options.text: Only needed in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Required in all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required in all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead is:

options.text: Not encouraged because it slows traffic.
Encouraged because it gives you time to react to hazards.
Only encouraged if you have a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged because it gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires keeping space on all sides of your vehicle. This space gives you time to respond if a problem occurs.

questions.question: You are most likely to encounter strong winds when:
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially common when leaving a tunnel.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not apply brakes if the vehicle is left out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. If needed, also block your wheels.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible when using a fire extinguisher. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are unsure which extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials fires, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts your mind and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving is safer than stopping. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: Being aware of what is happening behind you while driving is:
questions.explanation: It is important to know what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder as part of your normal driving routine.

questions.question: Headache racks:
questions.explanation: Headache racks protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Which of the following convictions disqualifies you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson disqualifies you from obtaining, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.
